blocks.text: Compose v2 (`docker compose`) declares services plus the networks, volumes, secrets and configs they use; every resource is prefixed by the project name.

blocks.code:
name: rag
services:
  api:
    build: .
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:8000:8000"]
    depends_on:
      db: { condition: service_healthy }
  db:
    image: pgvector/pgvector:pg17
    volumes: [pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data]
volumes:
  pgdata: {}

items: `compose.yaml` is the preferred filename; v1 `docker-compose` (Python) is end-of-life.

blocks.text: Renaming the folder (without `name:`) creates new, empty volumes; the old data sits under the old prefix. Two checkouts in same-named folders share containers and volumes.

Q: "Why did my database look empty after I moved the project folder?" A: "The project name defaulted to the directory name, and volumes are prefixed with it, so Compose created a new rag2_pgdata. The data is still in the old volume. Pin name: in compose.yaml."

items: Resources are prefixed by the project name.
